title: Henselianity of valuation coarsenings
statement: Let $K$ be a field and let $V\subseteq K$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$ [def-trf-valuation-ring]. Suppose that $V$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. If $U\subseteq K$ is another valuation ring with $V\subseteq U$, then $U$ is henselian. The inclusion $V\subseteq U$ is called a coarsening of valuations; $U=K$ is allowed. No rank, discreteness, completeness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374: valued-field background for the reference to Bourbaki, A.C., VI, §8. ILO supplies the motivating valued-field comparison, not a proof of this permanence theorem.
